auditedPrs.notes: Squash 8e2de14 on main, audited against github.com/tailscale/tailscale @ e2ed432399c9b0fda7aa14e9eb27784d2d893c55 (the pin PORTING.md documents), cloned shallow. The pong itself is faithful: Pong{TxID, Src: 127.3.3.40:<arrival region>} sealed to the ping's sender disco key, addressed to the DERP source node key, sent on the region the ping arrived on, nothing learned, region id truncated to u16 as Go does; a Geneve-framed disco frame over DERP goes to the dataplane on both sides. Five divergences remain around it, none inside the sealed frame: two in the reply path this PR added, two the PR left in the function it rewrote, and one in how the ping's sender is admitted (a single disco->node binding where Go accepts a set).

The 3 skipped are the socket-bound tests this box cannot run (serve_path_proxy_replays_consumed_head_to_backend and proxy_with_prefix_writes_prefix_before_bidi_copy hang on a dropped SYN, probe_stun_servers_once_sends_binding_request needs outbound UDP); they were filtered out rather than left to hang. The admission finding was checked separately on main at 225ea44 with the same bounds: clippy (both passes) clean; cargo nextest run -p geiserx_ts_magicsock -p geiserx_ts_runtime --all-features --no-fail-fast, 760 run, 753 passed, 7 failed, all seven ts_magicsock sock::tests timing out on a real loopback UDP socket this box blocks, with the 28 tests #472 added or rewrote passing; cargo build --workspace --exclude ts_cli_util --all-targets --all-features, clean.

findings.title: A DERP-relayed ping is only answered when the direct UDP socket bound
findings.detail: Upstream answers a disco ping received over DERP from the DERP reader itself: processDERPReadResult hands the frame to handleDiscoMessage -> handlePingLocked, which replies with sendDiscoMessage to the DERP address. Nothing on that path depends on the UDP socket being usable — when the UDP bind fails upstream substitutes blockForeverConn and the Conn, its DERP reader and its disco handling keep running. Here the pong is produced only inside MagicSock, and the DERP region runner reaches MagicSock only through Multiderp's direct_sock handle, which DirectManager installs (multiderp::SetDirectSock) only after a successful bind_underlay_addr; on bind failure DirectManager returns early with sock: None and never sends it. In that DERP-only posture — exactly the case this PR set out to fix, and the case where the peer has no other way to reach us — every relayed ping falls through to the dataplane as junk and the peer's `tailscale ping` times out just as it did before the change. The same hole is open as a startup race on a healthy node, between the first DERP connection and SetDirectSock being handled.
findings.upstream: wgengine/magicsock/derp.go @ e2ed432399c9b0fda7aa14e9eb27784d2d893c55 (processDERPReadResult; with wgengine/magicsock/magicsock.go handlePingLocked and wgengine/magicsock/blockforever_conn.go)

findings.title: A failed pong send tears down the whole region's DERP connection, and the send blocks the DERP reader
findings.detail: Upstream never sends disco from the DERP read path: handlePingLocked does `go c.sendDiscoMessage(...)`, which reaches sendAddr, which pushes a derpWriteRequest onto the region's write channel with a three-attempt, drop-oldest policy and returns errDropDerpPacket rather than blocking; the actual write happens in runDerpWriter, where a derp.Send error is logged (metricSendDERPError) and the writer loop continues. A pong that cannot be sent costs upstream exactly that pong. The merged code sends the reply inline in the region read loop — `client.send_one(to, &frame).await?` in run_derp_once — so a slow DERP write stalls inbound delivery for every peer on that region behind it, and any send error propagates out of run_derp_once, dropping the region's connection and putting it into the reconnect backoff. That teardown is reachable by any netmap peer simply by pinging this node over DERP.
findings.upstream: wgengine/magicsock/magicsock.go @ e2ed432399c9b0fda7aa14e9eb27784d2d893c55 (handlePingLocked reply, sendAddr; and wgengine/magicsock/derp.go runDerpWriter)

findings.title: A disco Pong relayed over DERP is still dropped, against the processDERPReadResult behaviour the diff cites
findings.detail: The PR cites processDERPReadResult for `what reaches the disco handler`, and upstream hands every non-Geneve disco frame over DERP to handleDiscoMessage — including a Pong, which is dispatched to endpoint.handlePongConnLocked. There the DERP case is explicit and live: the sentPing entry is removed, latency is computed from it and the CLI ping callback is fired (only the endpointState/bestAddr updates are guarded by !isDerp). That is how a node that pinged a peer over DERP completes its own `tailscale ping`. handle_relayed_disco still drops a relayed Pong, and the rewritten doc comment states the upstream rationale as `a Pong has no meaning without a matching ping we sent on this path` — true of this tree today only because nothing here ever sends a disco ping over DERP (Multiderp::send_disco has no caller in the workspace), not because upstream behaves that way. The reception side of the DERP ping/pong exchange is therefore half-ported, and the claim recorded in the code will mislead whoever ports the sending half.
findings.upstream: wgengine/magicsock/endpoint.go @ e2ed432399c9b0fda7aa14e9eb27784d2d893c55 (handlePongConnLocked; reached via wgengine/magicsock/derp.go processDERPReadResult)

findings.title: CallMeMaybe over DERP is still admitted on disco-key membership alone, not bound to the DERP source node key
findings.detail: Upstream's CallMeMaybe/CallMeMaybeVia arm refuses the frame unless the DERP source node key is itself a peer (`nodeKey := derpNodeSrc; ep, ok := c.peerMap.endpointForNodeKey(nodeKey)`), and then unless the sender's disco key belongs to that endpoint (`epDisco, knownKey := ep.checkAndUpdateDiscoKey(di.discoKey)`; `!knownKey` logs `CallMeMaybe from peer via DERP whose netmap discokey != disco source` and returns). The endpoints are applied to that node's endpoint. Here call_me_maybe_sender_allowed still calls the verifier with None, which verify_binding treats as membership-only — any peer's disco key that is in the netmap is accepted, and the endpoints are attributed by disco key with no reference to who the DERP server says sent the frame. This PR threads exactly the missing evidence (DerpSource) into this function and uses it only on the Ping arm. The gap is pre-existing rather than introduced, but it now sits one argument away from being closed: a peer that captured another peer's CallMeMaybe can replay it to us over DERP and have it acted on, which upstream refuses.

findings.title: DERP ping admission requires a single disco->node binding; Go accepts any known peer for derpNodeSrc
findings.detail: Upstream handlePingLocked over DERP pongs when the sender's disco key belongs to any known peer (handleDiscoMessage: peerMap.knownPeerDiscoKey(sender)) and derpNodeSrc resolves to any peer endpoint (numNodes = 1 if endpointForNodeKey(derpNodeSrc) ok); the disco->node relation is a set (peerMap.nodesOfDisco, 'Multiple nodes may share the same disco key in the case of node sharing and users switching accounts'). Merged answer_derp_ping asks verify(sender_disco, Some(derp_src_node_key)), which in ts_runtime::direct::verify_binding resolves the disco key through PeerDb::peer_by_known_disco_key (a HashMap<DiscoPublicKey, PeerId>, one peer per disco key) and requires that peer's node key to equal the DERP source. When two netmap nodes carry the same disco key (a shared node / one machine under two accounts), only the node that won the index slot gets a pong; the other's `tailscale ping` over DERP times out, the symptom the PR set out to remove. The PR's DECISIONS names only the cross-peer relay case as the deliberately stricter refusal and claims interop is unaffected; the shared-disco-key case is a real peer sealing with its own key. Inherited from the direct arm's verifier shape, but the PR ports the DERP arm onto it.
